## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

 const r=Math.hypot(x,z);

 h *= smoothstep(1.5,5.5,r)

}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D evolution/genetic simulator where creatures visibly evolve through mutation under biologically inspired selective pressures.
- User requested a build now with screenshots for self-checks; no clarifying questions.

## Requirements
- 3D game/simulator, creature evolution from mutation, grounded in real-life evolutionary principles.
- Must be complete/playable, visually polished, responsive.
- Save small JPEG screenshots at ≤1280px wide and only read the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Chose Vite + vanilla JS + Three.js.
- Built single-page “HELIX — Evolutionary Field Lab” with procedural 3D terrarium, 6-creature population, orbit camera, Bloom postprocessing.
- Creatures generated from a 10-gene genome; morphology includes body mass, neck, limbs, tail, armor, speed, fat, crest, pigment hue, pattern.
- Fitness components: thermal, forage, defense, efficiency; environment pressures alter selection weights.
- Evolution: rank survivors, weighted recombination, mutations, elite preservation, condition variance.
- Manual mutagen charges allow directed mutation, with +2 per generation up to 5.
- Added clutch of UI features: specimen dossier, trait bars with optimum markers, selection weights, fitness ring, field log, sparkline chart, population dots, auto-evolve at 1x/2x/4x, event toasts, field guide modal, reset, audio toggle.
- Added responsive mobile bottom sheets for specimen/ecology, touch-friendly controls, and mobile camera framing.
- Added 3D selection ring and floating creature name tag.
- Added WebAudio ambient pad/UI/mutation/evolution tones, muted by default.

- Project scaffold, dependencies, Vite build successfully.
- Full 3D world: floating island, pond, grass, ferns, trees, rocks, glowing crystals/mushrooms, fireflies, predator eyes, atmosphere, lights, shadows, bloom.
